source_name: CKB — audited consolidated financial statements 2024 (PDF)
why_relevant: Concrete PDF instance of the market leader's audited statements; notes typically carry fee-and-commission income splits that proxy card/acquiring volumes.

source_name: CKB — POS terminali (corporate acquiring product page)
why_relevant: Bank's own acquiring page states network size claims (POS terminal count, since 2002) and terminal/product capabilities — a rare entity-level POS estate disclosure outside the annual report.

source_name: CKB — TARIFNIK (fee schedule PDF)
why_relevant: Pricing disclosure: card issuance/maintenance fees, ATM withdrawal fees, merchant acquiring/POS rental fees — the pricing half of the cell brief and a leading indicator of acquiring economics.

source_name: NLB Banka AD Podgorica — Finansijski izvještaji
why_relevant: Second-largest bank in Montenegro (post NLB/Komercijalna merger). Publishes annual business reports, semi-annual/quarterly reports and Basel III 'Izvještaj o javnom objavljivanju' — the richest recurring disclosure set among ME banks, including digital-channel and card business narrative.

source_name: NLB Group — NLB Banka Podgorica market page
why_relevant: Parent-group English disclosure often quantifies subsidiary branch/ATM counts and digital-user metrics that the local site leaves in Montenegrin only; NLB Group annual report segments Montenegro.

source_name: Hipotekarna banka AD Podgorica — Godišnji izvještaji
why_relevant: Major domestically-owned bank, historically strong in card acquiring/issuing (Amex-style products, tourism merchant acquiring). Annual reports carry card and network narrative not available at regulator level.

source_name: Hipotekarna banka — Poslovnice i bankomati (branch & ATM locator)
why_relevant: Locator pages are a reveals-indirectly source: enumerating listed ATMs/branches yields a bottom-up estate count per bank, cross-checkable against annual-report claims and usable between report cycles.

source_name: Erste Bank AD Podgorica — Godišnji izvještaj banke
why_relevant: Erste ME is a leading retail/digital player; its annual report and Erste Group's Montenegro segment quantify card portfolios, mBanking/George users and network.

source_name: Erste Bank Montenegro — Tarife i naknade
why_relevant: Card, ATM and POS-acceptance pricing for a top-tier ME bank; comparable line-by-line with CKB/NLB tariffs for acquiring-price benchmarking.

source_name: Erste mBanking Crna Gora — app store listings (Google Play / App Store)
why_relevant: App-store install bands, rating counts, release notes and feature history are a proxy for digital-channel adoption and feature roadmap when banks do not publish mobile-user counts. Applies to every ME bank's app.

source_name: Lovćen banka AD Podgorica — Izvještaji o poslovanju
why_relevant: Mid-tier domestic bank (~5% market share) publishing annual and quarterly business reports; useful for the long tail of card/ATM estate and for tracking a fast-growing challenger.

source_name: Prva banka Crne Gore — Saopštenja / Kartice
why_relevant: Oldest ME bank (founded 1901) with domestic branch/ATM footprint; press-release page carries shareholder-meeting notices and financial-report announcements, and the cards page documents its issuing range.

source_name: Prva banka Crne Gore — bond prospectus filings on SCMN (Komisija za tržište kapitala)
why_relevant: Bond prospectuses are the richest bank-level disclosure format in Montenegro: business description typically includes client counts, card portfolio, branch/ATM network and channel strategy at a granularity annual reports omit.

source_name: Montenegroberza (Montenegro Stock Exchange) — issuer disclosure pages
why_relevant: Pointer/aggregator: banks that are listed issuers (or bond issuers) must file annual reports and material announcements with the exchange, giving one place to harvest bank-level reports without visiting eleven bank sites.

source_name: Adriatic Bank AD Podgorica — Reports / financial statements
why_relevant: Newer (2016) niche bank with strong income growth; its audited statements and management reports document its card/e-banking build-out — relevant for challenger-side terminal and card demand.

source_name: Bankar.me — sector and bank-by-bank business analyses; ATM/branch directory
why_relevant: Specialist ME banking portal that periodically ranks all banks by assets/market share and publishes card-usage numbers (e.g. payment-card counts and ATM totals); also maintains a bank branch/ATM location directory. Useful as a cross-check and as a pointer to bank disclosures.

source_name: CompanyWall Montenegro — bank company financial profiles
why_relevant: Commercial registry aggregator carrying revenue, headcount and filing metadata per bank legal entity; useful to date filings and to catch entities whose own sites publish little (e.g. Ziraat, Universal Capital, Zapad).

source_name: TheBanks.eu — Montenegro bank profiles (Lovćen, Universal Capital, etc.)
why_relevant: English-language normalized profiles giving assets, market share and rank per ME bank; convenient for sizing/weighting banks before deciding which annual reports to mine.

source_name: Wikipedia — List of banks in Montenegro (actor map seed)
why_relevant: Quick bilingual actor map with ownership/parent-group mapping (OTP, NLB, Erste, Ziraat) that tells you which foreign parent annual reports also segment Montenegro. Must be validated against the CBCG register.

source_name: CBCG — Registar institucija za elektronski novac i njihovih agenata (Register of E-money Institutions)
why_relevant: Statutory register of e-money issuers, their branches and agents. As observed, the register currently states no e-money institution is entered — itself a first-order market fact (no domestic e-money licensee in Montenegro), and the page is the tripwire that will show the first entrant.

source_name: CBCG — Spisak platnih institucija i institucija za elektronski novac kojima je oduzeto odobrenje (revoked authorisations list)
why_relevant: Negative-space companion to the registers: identifies exits, failed fintechs and supervisory enforcement, which is how you distinguish market churn from market growth and reconstruct the historical population of licensees.

source_name: CBCG — Registri (payment-system registers index)
why_relevant: Hub page enumerating all four statutory payment registers (payment systems, payment institutions, e-money institutions, revoked authorisations). Stable entry point that will surface any newly created register (e.g. a future crypto/VASP or PISP register) without needing new discovery.

source_name: CBCG — Finansijski izvještaji platnih institucija i institucija za elektronski novac / Pružaoci finansijskih usluga
why_relevant: Supervisory-function section referenced as hosting financial reports of payment institutions and e-money institutions alongside those of banks and other financial-service providers. Firm-level financials (revenue, fee income, volumes) are the way to size individual non-bank payment players rather than only counting them. Exact sub-page URL for the payment-institution reports was not confirmed by direct fetch, so treat the path as approximate.
